nodes.text: Let $h(n)$ be such that, for any set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of size $n$, the set\[\left\{ \frac{a}{(a,b)}: a,b\in A\right\}\]has size at least $h(n)$. Estimate $h(n)$.

#539 : [Er73,p.125] additive combinatorics | number theory Erdős and Szemerédi proved that\[n^{1/2} \ll h(n) \ll n^{1-c}\]for some constant $c>0$. The upper bound has been improved to $h(n)\ll n^{2/3}$ by Freiman and Lev. A proof of these bounds can be found in a paper of Granville and Roesler [GrRo99] . Granville and Roesler also reformulate this problem as one in combinatorial geometry: given $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ of size $n$ what is the minimum size possible of\[\{ \delta(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b}) : \mathbf{a},\mathbf{b}\in A\}\]where $\delta(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b})$ has $i$th coordinate $\max(0,a_i-b_i)$. Using this formulation they obtained improved lower bounds in fixed small dimension $d$. Using this reformulation, ProofCouncil has proved that\[h(n) \leq e^{O(\sqrt{\log n})} n^{1/2},\]and hence $h(n)=n^{1/2+o(1)}$.
